title: Cryptool vs CoinTracker
content_html:
If you need tax reports for many crypto trades, CoinTracker is a good fit. If you need to run a fund, raise capital, or manage a syndicate, Cryptool.io is the better fit. cryptool vs cointracker is a comparison between a full crypto investment operating system and a consumer portfolio tracker that focuses on tax reporting.

What CoinTracker is good at

CoinTracker tracks balances and transactions from many wallets and exchanges. It pulls data automatically once a wallet or exchange is linked. It shows a clear list of assets, buys, sells, and transfers. It calculates cost basis and gains for tax reporting. It can export tax forms that many accountants accept. It works well for individuals who trade on a few exchanges and need a simple tax report. It supports many major chains and exchange APIs. It does not require users to run their own nodes. It offers a clean web dashboard and mobile app. It is a non-custodial tool that never holds any crypto for the user.

What Cryptool does differently

Cryptool.io tracks holdings across any number of wallets from any provider. It updates balances automatically on all supported chains. It lets users add multiple wallets and see the total portfolio in one view. It goes beyond tracking by letting users manage investments, allocate capital, and run fund books. It includes investor CRM features that record commitments and communications. It supports venture capital workflows such as deal pipelines and token vesting schedules. It lets syndicates set per-member allocations and run capital raises end to end. It provides an OTC marketplace for off-exchange trades. It records token distributions and generates investor reports. It adds a shared calendar for raise dates, vesting events, and portfolio milestones. In short, Cryptool combines portfolio tracking with fund administration, investor management, and deal workflow in a single non-custodial platform.

Which one should you pick

Choose CoinTracker if you are an individual trader who wants automatic transaction import, cost-basis calculation, and ready-to-file tax forms. Choose CoinTracker if you trade on a few exchanges and need a simple view of your current holdings without extra workflow features. Choose Cryptool.io if you run a crypto fund, a syndicate, or any organized investment group that needs to track multiple wallets, manage allocations, run raises, and keep investor records. Choose Cryptool.io if you need token vesting schedules, OTC trade logs, or a shared calendar for fund events. In many cases, a user may start with CoinTracker for tax reporting and later add Cryptool.io when the investment process grows beyond simple tracking.

FAQ

What is the main difference between cryptool and cointracker?

cryptool provides a full investment operating system with fund administration, investor CRM, and deal workflow, while cointracker focuses on portfolio tracking and tax reporting for individual traders.

Does cointracker support multi-wallet tracking on all chains?

Yes, cointracker can connect many wallets and exchanges and shows balances across supported chains, but it does not include fund-level features.

Can cryptool generate tax reports like cointracker?

Cryptool does not focus on tax reporting. Users who need detailed tax forms should use a dedicated tax tool such as cointracker.

Is cryptool non-custodial like cointracker?

Yes, cryptool is non-custodial. Users keep control of their private keys and add wallets without handing over custody.

Where can I learn more about setting up multi-wallet tracking in cryptool?

You can follow the step-by-step guide on multi-wallet portfolio tracking on all chains: [step-by-step guide](/blog/step-by-step-guide-to-setting-up-multi-wallet-portfolio-trac).

How does cryptool help with investor reporting for syndicates?

Cryptool records each investor's commitment, allocation, and communication, then produces reports that can be shared with LPs or syndicate members. For a deeper look at LP reporting, see the guide on managing LP reporting for crypto syndicates: [LP reporting guide](/blog/how-to-manage-lp-reporting-for-crypto-syndicates-step-by-ste).
